title: No evaluation CLI: scoring a pipeline requires starting a training run
description: The only end-to-end scorer is TUNetDetectorTrainer._score_fold, which is private and reached only by launching training. There is no way to ask "what does this detector + linker + post-proc chain + threshold score on fold N". That gap is what stopped DivisionRecovery being validated on real detections rather than ground-truth nodes. Build celltrack/evaluate.py taking a LinkerConfig, a post-proc chain and a read-out threshold, reusing ValidationFold and the existing local evaluator, and reporting edge_jaccard / division_jaccard / score the way bracket.py now does.
acceptance_criteria: One command scores celltrack-pilktunet-motion-stlf on fold 0 and reproduces the recorded 0.877, then scores the divstlf variant for comparison.
notes: Unlocks three queued things at once: validating divisions end to end (GT-node ceiling was +0.045, real detections will differ because unparented false positives are far more common); the 0.5 -> 0.95 detection threshold sweep, already measured at +0.009 on full-41 and never shipped; and gap-close (stlfg) after that. All the inputs now exist locally - pack weights, external/ source and the data root are wired via junctions.

title: Periodic validation + best-checkpoint selection during training
description: run.py logs only first/last train loss (run.losses[0] -> run.losses[-1]). There is no held-out eval during training, no early stopping, and the weights saved are whatever the final step produced - not the best. We cannot tell whether a long run is still improving or has started overfitting. Add --val-every N running the existing local evaluator on a held-out subset, log the curve to MLflow alongside loss, and keep best.pt separately from last.pt.
acceptance_criteria: A training run emits a validation curve in MLflow and writes a best.pt that differs from last.pt when the run degrades.
close_reason: Already provided by the trainer: --eval-every periodic fold-0 subset scoring + save-best-checkpoint (train() keeps best-by-score). No separate work needed.

description: celltrack/training/loop.py has no checkpointing: run.py saves weights only at the very end, after --steps. title: Fix plateau NMS in peaks.py (max-pool marks every voxel of a flat blob)
description: peaks._local_maxima uses volume==maxpool(volume): on a SATURATED detector the response is flat plateaus at prob~1, so EVERY voxel of a plateau equals the neighbourhood max -> ~1e5 'peaks'/frame (measured 100476/frame on aug@0.99, 528k/163k on above_threshold evals). title: Operating-point sweep: N_pred/N_total against realised score
description:
The adjustment ratio is signed and uncapped above, so predicting FEWER nodes than the estimated true
count multiplies the jaccard by more than 1 (up to 1.1). Detecting every cell earns exactly 1.0.

That argument is arithmetic on the formula, not an experiment. Sweep the detector's threshold across
N_pred/N_total and measure the realised score, per prefix - the aggregation weights each video by
its own TP+FP+FN, so the bonus is worth most where annotation is densest (6bba), which is also where
N_total is smallest and the ratio moves fastest.

title: Detection model: 3D U-Net with temporal context
description:
Per-voxel detection map over an anisotropic volume, cell centres recovered by local-maximum
suppression with an NMS radius derived from the physics (voxel spacing + measured cell scale), not
tuned by hand.

Anisotropy is 4x: an isotropic kernel in index space is an ellipsoid in the tissue. Either use
anisotropic kernels/strides or resample - decide with an argument, and record it.

bracket task at a matched node count, on the held-out prefix split.

title: Linking model: candidate generation plus learned scoring
description:
Candidates are generated with a radius that covers the measured motion tail (median 1.82 um/frame,
p99 8.38, max 60.8) - deliberately WIDER than the 7 um matching cutoff, so the scorer has real
competitors to discriminate rather than a single obvious partner. Then a learned pairwise score over
consecutive frames, resolved into a one-to-one assignment (plus the two-child case at divisions).

DONE WHEN: it beats nearest-neighbour linking on ground-truth nodes - i.e. it exceeds the ceiling
from the bracket task, which is exactly the number nearest-neighbour cannot pass.

Composes NN one-to-one then attaches unmatched daughters to nearest matched parent within a tight 7um division radius (=matching cutoff; wider gates add false divisions). Exceeds the bracket ceiling = DONE-WHEN. Note: real score bottleneck is detection jitter, not GT-node linking (see operating-point-sweep). title: Half-precision the response cache via fp16 logits (not probs, never bf16)
description:
ResponseCache is fp32 because the equality-NMS (volume==max_pool) breaks under fp16-of-PROBABILITIES: probs saturate near 1.0 where fp16 ULP~0.0005, so distinct peaks (0.99998 vs 0.99991) round equal -> false plateau -> merged detection -> replay 0.8160 vs live 0.9090 (see commit 24a8f15).

FIX (normalization, per user insight): cache LOGITS (pre-sigmoid), not probabilities. sigmoid is monotonic so max_pool equality NMS yields identical peaks; logits DON'T saturate (peaks land at logit~9-11, fp16 ULP~0.008 there = resolvable). Threshold t remaps to logit(t) e.g. 0.99->4.595; background very-negative logits filtered by the >floor cut. Result: fp16 storage + faithful NMS + half disk.

bf16 is EXCLUDED: 8-bit mantissa, ULP near 1.0 ~0.004 (8x coarser than fp16) — corrupts MORE.

PRIORITY LOW: payoff is disk only. Cache-replay bottleneck is CPU peak-extract+link (~1.4s/video), not disk load; fp32->fp16 saves ~1-2s on a ~57s replay. Storage precision is NOT the experimentation-speed lever (the cache EXISTING is). Do this only if the cache becomes disk/load-bound. Acceptance: fp16-logit cache reproduces 0.9090 local fold-0 exactly (bit-faithful peaks vs fp32).
